author: iFixit
description:
Apple’s Homeview looks like a familiar mix of iPad and HomePod. Inside, stubborn adhesive and fragile connectors turn this teardown into a fight.

We start with a CT scan, then work through the display, A18 logic board, speakers, and base to see what stands between a broken Homeview and a successful repair. Along the way: speaker connectors that come apart during disconnection, a heat spreader bonded to the chassis, and a speaker that breaks during removal.

There are a few bright spots, including a modular USB-C port. We also open the wall-mounted version to find out why its board and speakers differ from the freestanding model.

After the repair progress we’ve seen in iPads and HomePods, how did Homeview end up here?

Which design choice would you change first to make Homeview easier to repair?
